sanskrit: suparṇas tvānvavindat sūkaras tvākhanan nasā | dipsauṣadhe tvaṃ dipsantaṃ prati kṛtyākṛto daha ||
english: The eagle found you out; the boar dug you up with his snout. O herb that harms the harmer — you who would harm us — burn back the maker of the sorcery.

sanskrit: prati daha yātudhānān prati kṛtyākṛto daha | atho yo asmān dipsati tam u tvaṃ jahy oṣadhe ||
english: Burn back the sorcerers, burn back the maker of the sorcery. And whoever seeks to harm us — him, too, do you strike down, O herb.

sanskrit: agne pṛtanāṣāṭ pṛtanāḥ sahasva | prati kṛtyāṃ kṛtyākṛte pratiharaṇena harāmasi ||
english: O Agni, crusher of armies, overpower the armies. We carry the sorcery back to the sorcerer by means of this counter-charm.

sanskrit: iṣvā ṛjīyaḥ patatu dyāvāpṛthivī tat sutāt | tat taṃ mṛga iva vidhyatu kṛtyā kṛtyākṛtaṃ kṛtā ||
english: Straight as an arrow may it fly. Heaven and Earth — let them press it out. May the sorcery, thus fashioned, pierce its maker as an arrow pierces a beast.

sanskrit: agham astv aghakṛte śapathāḥ śapathīvne | pratyak prati pra hiṇmasi yaś cakāra tam ṛcchatu ||
english: Let evil befall the evil-doer; let curses befall the curser. We send them back, forward and straight — let them find the one who fashioned them.

sanskrit: yas tvā kṛtya ity ekā ||
english: "He who has sorcery done to him" — this is the single verse.

sanskrit: punaḥ kṛtyāṃ kṛtyākṛte hastagṛhya parā ṇaya | samakṣam asmā ā dadhmo yathā kṛtyākṛtaṃ hanat ||
english: Seizing the sorcery by the hand, carry it back again to the sorcerer. We place it full in his presence, that it may slay the sorcery's maker.

sanskrit: putra iva pitaraṃ gaccha svaja ivābhiṣṭhito daśa | tantur ivāvavyayann ihi kṛtye kṛtyākṛtaṃ kṛtā ||
english: Go to him as a son to his father; cling and bite as a serpent coiled around its prey. Come unwinding like a thread, O sorcery fashioned — strike the sorcery's maker.

sanskrit: ud eṇīva vāriṇy abhiskandaṃ mṛgīva | kṛtyā kartāram ṛcchatu ||
english: As a doe leaps up into the water, as a female deer leaps forth — so may the sorcery find its maker.

sanskrit: ṛśyasyeva parīśāsaṃ parimāya pari tvacaḥ | durhārde cakruṣe kṛtyāṃ grīvāsu prati muñcata ||
english: Measuring around like the hide of a spotted deer, encircling the skin — fasten the sorcery back around the necks of those with evil hearts who performed it.

sanskrit: yā kṛtye devakṛtā yā vā manuṣyajā asi | tāṃ tvā prati pra hiṇmasi pratīcīnena brahmaṇā ||
english: Whether you, O sorcery, were fashioned by gods or were born of men — we send you back with this counter-formula directed against the source.

sanskrit: yadi strī yadi vā pumān kṛtyāṃ cakāra pāpmane | tām u tasmai nayāmasy aśvam ivāśvābhidhānyā ||
english: Whether a woman or a man performed the sorcery for the sake of harm — we lead it back to that one, as a mare-tether leads a horse.

sanskrit: okte me dyāvā pṛthivī oktā devī sarasvatī | oktau ma indraś cāgniś ca krimiṃ jambhayatām imam ||
english: Heaven and Earth have been invoked for me; the divine Sarasvatī has been invoked. Both Indra and Agni have been invoked for me — may they crush this worm.

sanskrit: asyendra kumārasya krimiṃ dhanapate jahi | hatā viśvā arātayo 'nena vacasā mama ||
english: O Indra, O Lord of Wealth, slay the worm of this boy. Slain are all adversaries by this utterance of mine.

sanskrit: yo +'kṣyau parisarpati yo nāse parisarpati | datāṃ yo madhyaṃ gacchati taṃ krimiṃ jambhayāmasi ||
english: The one that creeps around the eyes, the one that creeps around the nostrils, the one that goes into the middle of the teeth — that worm we crush.

sanskrit: virūpau dvau sarūpau dvau kṛṣṇau dvau rohitau dvau | babhruś ca babhrukarṇaś ca gṛdhrāḥ kokāś ca te hatāḥ ||
english: Two of unlike form, two of like form, two black ones, two reddish ones; the tawny one and the tawny-eared one; vultures and crows — these are slain.

sanskrit: ye krimayaḥ śitikakṣā ye kṛṣṇāḥ śitibāhavaḥ | ye ke ca viśvarūpās tān krimīñ jambhayāmasi ||
english: The worms that have white armpits, those that are black with white arms, and whatever they are of all various forms — those worms we crush.

sanskrit: yo dviśīrṣā caturakṣaḥ krimiḥ sāraṅgo arjunaḥ | śṛṇāmy asya pṛṣṭīr api vṛścāmi yac chiraḥ ||
english: The worm that is two-headed and four-eyed, the speckled one, the white one — I shatter its ribs and I cut off its head.

sanskrit: ud asau sūryo agād viśvadṛṣṭo adṛṣṭahā | dṛṣṭāṃś ca ghnann adṛṣṭāṃś ca sarvāṃś ca pramṛṇan krimīn ||
english: That sun has risen, visible to all, the slayer of the unseen. Striking those that are seen and those unseen, crushing all worms altogether.

sanskrit: yevāṣāsaḥ kaṣkaṣāso dhrūkṣṇāsaḥ śipavitnavaḥ | dṛṣṭaś ca hanyatāṃ krimir adṛṣṭaś cota hanyatām ||
english: The yevāṣas, the kaṣkaṣas, the dhrūkṣṇas, the śipavitnus — let the worm that is seen be slain, and let the worm that is unseen be slain as well.

sanskrit: hato yevāṣo hataḥ śipavir hato gaṅgaṇivām̐ uta | hatā viśvā arātaya ugreṇa vacasā mama ||
english: Slain is the yevāṣa, slain the śipavit, slain likewise the gaṅgaṇi. Slain are all adversaries by my fierce utterance.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ ca krimīṇāṃ sarvāsāṃ ca krimīṇām | bhinadmy aśmanā śiro dahāmy agninā mukham ||
english: Of all worms, male and female alike — I split the head with a stone, I burn the mouth with fire.

sanskrit: tigmebhir agne arcibhiḥ śukreṇa deva śociṣā | āmādo ni vaha tvam anyam āsani kṛṇvatām ||
english: With your sharp flames, O Agni, with your bright blazing light, O god — carry away the raw-flesh eater; make him settle his mouth elsewhere.

sanskrit: śociṣāgne arciṣā ca nir daheto aghāyataḥ | sakhyam āvaṃ kṛṇvahe tvaṃ ca- -āmāda upa śaṃ bhuvan ||
english: With your blazing light and your flame, O Agni, burn out the evil-doer. Let the two of us forge a friendship, and may the raw-flesh eater be at peace — elsewhere.

sanskrit: nir āmādo nayāmasi niṣ kravyādo gṛhebhyaḥ | sasyādo nāma ye deva te agne mā dabhan tvām ||
english: We lead forth the raw-flesh eater, we lead forth the carrion eater from the houses. Those gods called the grain-eaters, O Agni — may they not harm you.

sanskrit: āmādaś ca kravyādaś ca sasyādaś cobhayān saha | prajāṃ ye cakrire bhāgaṃ tān ito nir ṇayāmasi ||
english: The raw-flesh eater and the carrion eater and the grain-eater — both kinds together — those who have made offspring their share, them we lead forth from here.

sanskrit: ya āmeṣv aramanta na pakvam upadādhṛṣuḥ | te yantu sarve saṃbhūya- -anyatreto 'ghāyavaḥ ||
english: Those who take pleasure in raw things, who have not stooped to the cooked — let all of them gather together and go hence, the evil-doers, to another place.

sanskrit: ya enasvī duṣkṛtakṛt kilbiṣakṛtasādhī yaḥ | punas tān yajñiyā devā nayantu yata āgatāḥ ||
english: He who is sinful, a doer of evil deeds, he whose success is made of transgression — may the gods worthy of sacrifice lead them back whence they have come.

sanskrit: ava reṇum ava rajo neneje hastyaṃ malam | dhātā no bhadrayā neṣat sa no gopāyatu prajām ||
english: Wash away the dust, wash away the impurity; cleanse the filth belonging to the elephant. May Dhātṛ lead us with good fortune; may he protect our offspring.

sanskrit: kṛṇve 'haṃ rodasī varma syāma savituḥ save | mātā no bhadrayā bhūmir dyauś cāsmān pātv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: I make of Heaven and Earth my armor; may we be in the impulsion of Savitṛ. May Earth, our mother, with good fortune, and Heaven protect us from distress.

sanskrit: yad asurāṇām ahany asmān pāpā upethana | devānāṃ payaś ca daivyam āpaḥ śundhantu mām imāḥ ||
english: Whatever evil things belonging to the Asuras have approached us on those days — may the milk of the gods and these divine waters cleanse me.

sanskrit: ā te pitar marutāṃ sumnam emi mā naḥ sūryasya saṃdṛśo yuvathāḥ | abhi no vīro 'rvatīḥ kṣameta pra jāyāmahai rudra prajayā ||
english: I come to your grace, O father of the Maruts; keep us not away from the sight of the Sun. May the hero prevail for us in the contests of steeds; may we propagate, O Rudra, with offspring.

sanskrit: yo 'vṛddhaṃ hanti yo garbhe antar yo jātaṃ janitavyaṃ ca pūruṣam | tasmā ṛdhyāsaṃ haviṣāham adya sa naḥ prajāṃ jaradaṣṭiṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: He who slays the unborn, he who is within the womb, he who slays the man already born or yet to be born — may I prosper against him today with oblation; may he grant us offspring that lives to old age.
